title: Mulligan
attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the item; The Mulligan] 

Mulligans are enemies that will actively try to avoid Isaac; their eyes widen and their speed increases when doing so. When running away, they may walk over spikes or into a fire.

Upon death, they spawn several Fly, Attack Fly and, occasionally, a Pooter. Mulligans may sometimes self-detonate. If this occurs: in addition to spawning flies as normal, it will also fire four projectiles in the cardinal directions and destroy nearby objects when doing so. Mulligans cannot deal contact damage to Isaac ( [Before Afterbirth+] unless they are Champions).

Alternatively, if a Mulligan's health is dropped to -10 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Mulligoon
sections.text: Mulligoons behave like Mulligans and will run away from Isaac, don't deal contact damage, and can self-detonate. They release 4 projectiles in ordinal directions and drop a Troll Bomb on death. If they self-detonate, they release 8 projectiles in the cardinal and ordinal directions in addition to dropping a Troll bomb.

sections.heading: Mulliboom
sections.text: Mullibooms, unlike Mulligans, will chase Isaac at a very fast pace and explode on contact, dealing half a heart of damage. They also explode immediately if they are killed.

sections.heading: Hive
sections.text:
Hives behave similarly to Mulligans, evading Isaac and spawning Fly, Attack Fly, and Pooters upon death. However, they also occasionally spit Attack Fly while running away from Isaac, and unlike Mulligans and Mulligoons, they can't self-detonate.

Alternatively, if a Hive's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Drowned Hive
sections.text:
Drowned Hives behave similarly to Hives but spit out Drowned Chargers instead of Attack Flies. Upon death, they spawn 1-2 Drowned Chargers.

Alternatively, if a Drowned Hive's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

[Repentance] Drowned Chargers spawned by Drowned Hives have half their usual health (11 HP).

sections.heading: Nest
sections.text:
Nests behave similarly to Hives, but they spit out Spider instead of Attack Fly when being chased. They spawn a Trite or a Big Spider upon death.

Unlike normal Spider, those spawned by the Nest die upon touching Isaac. This is not the case for spiders spawned from killing the Big spider.

Alternatively, if a Nest's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Leper
sections.text:
Lepers are a Mulligan variant that alternate between walking towards and running away from Isaac. For every 15 damage they take, a chunk of their head, known as a Leper Flesh, will detach and start erratically chasing Isaac. Lepers deal contact damage if they are in this state or below. Lepers can naturally be found with some head chunks missing.

After being reduced to 15 health, Lepers will chase Isaac continuously, leaving a trail of damaging Red Creep. Upon death, they leave behind one Leper Flesh and have a 50% chance to leave behind a Grey-colored Gusher.

Alternatively, if a Leper's health is dropped to -25 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will never spawn a Gusher on death, but will still spawn Leper Flesh.

sections.heading: Leper Flesh
sections.text:
Leper Fleshes are head chunks from Lepers that erratically chase Isaac and are spawned from Lepers for every 15 damage they take. Upon death, they fire a projectile at Isaac that predicts his movements.

They will die if Isaac walks into them, though he will still take contact damage.

sections.heading: Holy Mulligan
sections.text:
Holy Mulligans behave similarly to Nests and Hives; avoiding Isaac and spawning Angelic Baby (small) when chased. When killed, they leave behind 1-2 Embryos.

Alternatively, if a Holy Mulligan's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Prey
sections.text:
Preys behave similarly to Nests and Hives; avoiding Isaac and spawning Small Leeches when chased. Upon death, they spawn 2-3 Small Leeches.

Alternatively, if a Prey's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Mullighoul
sections.text:
Mullighouls behave similarly to Nests and Hives; avoiding Isaac and occasionally spawning a Willo when chased. Upon death it spawns 1-2 Willos. This variant can fly over pits.

Alternatively, if a Mullighoul's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Gas Dwarf
sections.text: Gas Dwarves act similar to Mullibooms, but hock up explosive gas as they chase Isaac. Upon death, they release an explosive Ipecac shot that blows up any gas clouds it hits. If it manages to reach Isaac, however, it will explode, damaging Isaac and detonating nearby gas clouds.

sections.heading: Bouncer
sections.text:
Bouncers behave like regular Mulligans and avoid Isaac with the exception that they can still deal contact damage to Isaac in their normal state. However, after some time or when close to death, their head inflates and they start chasing Isaac. If they die or come into contact with him in this state, they explode into a large cloud of projectiles with some lingering in the air before dropping down. If they are killed before they enter this hostile state, they release 4 projectiles in the ordinal directions.

They can also occasionally reflect tears in their inflated state.

sections.heading: Tainted Mulligan
sections.text:
Tainted Mulligans are stronger versions of Mulligans that behave similarly to Hives. They walk away from Isaac and will spit several Ring Fly at him if he is near. Upon death, they spawn a plethora of fly enemies including: Fly, Attack Fly, Suckers, Spits, Inks, Boom Fly, and Red Boom Fly.

Alternatively, if a Tainted Mulligan's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

They are exclusive to the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Leper and Leper Flesh enemies were added in Booster Pack #5.

• The Mulligan, Mulligoon, Hive, and Swarmer are all the same monster in stages of decay and infestation.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, when a Mulligan self-detonated, the explosion would not break rocks.

• Mulligans will start running in random directions instead of directly away from Isaac if he stays close to them for long enough. This behavior also applies to Small Baby Long Legs.

• In the game's files, there is an unused Mulliboom self-detonation animation, an unused graphic of a Hive with a Mulligoon's face, and an unused graphic of the [Afterbirth onward] Drowned Hive with a blue-tinted Mulligoon's face.

• [Afterbirth onward] Drowned Hives, along with Drowned Chargers (name of Drowned Charger wasn't revealed), were revealed for Afterbirth in this official Binding of Isaac post.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] A leper is a person who suffers from leprosy, which is a contagious disease that causes discoloration and lumping on the skin plus disfigurement and deformities.

• [Repentance] Due to the Holy Mulligan leaving behind Embryos on death, it could be suggested that it transforms Embryos into the Small Angelic Babies it spawns.

• [Repentance] Holy Mulligans, Holy Bony, and Holy Eyes originated as cards from the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls.

• [Repentance] Gas Dwarves used to be called Fartigans.

• [Repentance] Prey, Mullighouls, and Bouncers originate from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Mullighouls could also appear in Mausoleum and had 13 stage hp. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If a Mulligan or a Mulligoon is killed before the spawning period is finished (before they move), it will count as a self-detonation.
Bug note: If a Nest is killed in the Burning Basement, it has a chance to spawn a Flaming Hopper.
Bug note: Rarely if you kill a Drowned Hive before their spawn period is finished (before they move), it will shoot 4 projectiles in ordinal directions but the monster won't explode.
